**AI 380: Human-AI Interaction · Willamette University**

**Project:** `AppCoach_demo`, the App Coach assistant from Lab 3, finished and tested with `rasa inspect`.

**Outcome:** The assistant runs in Docker on an Azure VM and is reachable at `https://<your-name>.<region>.cloudapp.azure.com`, **behind a password**.

## 🛠️ How to use this workshop

1. Read the concept.
2. Run the command or create the named file.
3. Pass the checkpoint.
4. Continue only when it passes.

::: {.checkpoint}
**Starting point:** `AppCoach_demo` works in `rasa inspect` on your laptop. Nothing else is assumed: no web page, no Dockerfile, no extra code.
:::

## ✅ Seven things you will do

1. 📋 Check the project is ready to ship.
2. 🧱 Add the deploy files (Compose, Caddy, `.env.example`).
3. 🧪 Run the official Rasa image locally against your project.
4. 🐙 Push the project to GitHub.
5. ☁️ Create the Azure VM and install Docker.
6. 🚀 Pull, add secrets, train, and start with HTTPS.
7. 🔎 Verify, update, stop, and clean up.

## 📦 What gets deployed

| Piece | Where it comes from | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Rasa Pro | Official Rasa Pro Docker image | **No custom Dockerfile** |
| Your assistant | The repo, mounted into the container | `domain.yml`, `data/`, `actions/`, `config.yml`, `endpoints.yml`, `credentials.yml` |
| Custom actions | Run **inside** Rasa (`actions_module`) | No separate action server |
| Trained model | Built on the VM with `rasa train` | `models/` is not in git |
| HTTPS and password | Caddy container | Free certificate; browser login prompt |
| `lesson_log.jsonl` | Written in the project folder on the VM | Survives restarts |

## 🌐 Do you need a web page?

**No.** `rasa run --inspect` serves the **Inspector**, the same chat, Flow, History, and Memory view you used locally, over the REST channel.

| Option | Use it when |
|---|---|
| **Inspector (this workshop)** | Demos, grading, debugging a deployed assistant |
| Custom page (for example `web_test.html`) | You want a friendlier or branded interface for end users |

> The Inspector is a **developer tool**. That is why this deck puts a password in front of it.

## 🔒 Why HTTPS and a password

- Browsers allow the **microphone** only on `https://` or `localhost`.
- The assistant calls a paid **LLM** with your key. An open URL lets strangers spend it.
- `lesson_log.jsonl` records user IDs and replies.

Caddy gives you both: a free certificate **and** a login prompt before anything reaches Rasa.

## 📋 Prerequisites

- `AppCoach_demo` runs with `rasa train` and `rasa inspect`.
- A **Rasa Pro license** key and your **LLM API key**.
- [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/) installed and running.
- [GitHub Desktop](https://desktop.github.com/) and a GitHub account.
- An Azure account (Part 4).
- A terminal: **PowerShell** on Windows, **Terminal** on macOS.

## ① Prepare the project {.section-slide background-color="#087e80"}

::: {.eyebrow}
Parts 1–3 · Check, package, test locally
:::

**Ready → Compose files → official image on your laptop**

## 📋 Part 1 · Is the project ready?

Your project folder should look like this:

```text
AppCoach_demo/
├── actions/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── actions.py
│   └── lessons.py
├── data/
│   ├── flows.yml
│   └── patterns.yml
├── domain.yml
├── config.yml
├── endpoints.yml
├── credentials.yml
└── models/            (trained locally; NOT committed)
```

## 🔍 Part 1 · Four things to confirm

| Check | Why |
|---|---|
| `rasa --version` | Write it down. Use the **same version** for the Docker image |
| `endpoints.yml` has `action_endpoint: actions_module: "actions"` | Actions run inside Rasa; no action server to deploy |
| `credentials.yml` contains `rest:` | `rasa run --inspect` attaches the Inspector to the REST channel |
| Secrets are not in any file | The license and LLM key come from environment variables |

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint 1:** `rasa train` and `rasa inspect` both work, and you have the version number.
:::

## 🧱 Part 2 · Add the deploy files

Create a `deploy/` folder in the project root:

```text
AppCoach_demo/
└── deploy/
    ├── docker-compose.yml
    ├── Caddyfile
    └── .env.example
```

All three are safe to commit. The real `deploy/.env` is **not** committed.

## 📝 2.1 · `deploy/docker-compose.yml`

```yaml
services:
  assistant:
    image: europe-west3-docker.pkg.dev/rasa-releases/rasa-pro/rasa-pro:3.18.0
    command: ["run", "--inspect"]
    restart: unless-stopped
    user: root
    env_file: .env
    volumes:
      - ..:/app

  caddy:
    image: caddy:2
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    environment:
      DOMAIN: ${DOMAIN}
      AUTH_USER: ${AUTH_USER}
      AUTH_HASH: ${AUTH_HASH}
    volumes:
      - ./Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro
      - caddy_data:/data
    depends_on:
      - assistant

volumes:
  caddy_data:
```

## 🔍 Read the Compose file

| Line | Why |
|---|---|
| `image: ...rasa-pro:3.18.0` | Official image. **Change the tag to your tested version** |
| `command: ["run", "--inspect"]` | Start the server with the Inspector |
| `..:/app` | Mount your project into the container. Models, actions, and the log live in your folder |
| `user: root` | Same as Rasa's official template, so the container can write `models/` and the log |
| No `ports:` on `assistant` | Only Caddy is exposed to the internet |

::: {.notes}
Rasa's own quick-deploy template uses this image path, a bind mount of the project, and user root. Verify the image path and latest tag on Rasa's Docker install page before class.
:::

## 📝 2.2 · `deploy/Caddyfile`

```text
{$DOMAIN} {
	basic_auth {
		{$AUTH_USER} {$AUTH_HASH}
	}
	reverse_proxy assistant:5005
}
```

For the site name in `DOMAIN`: get a certificate, ask for a login, then forward to Rasa on port 5005.

The password is stored only as a **hash** in `.env`, never as plain text.

## 📝 2.3 · `deploy/.env.example`

```text
# Copy to .env and fill in. Never commit .env.
RASA_LICENSE=your-rasa-pro-license
OPENAI_API_KEY=your-llm-key
DOMAIN=localhost
AUTH_USER=coach
AUTH_HASH='paste-the-caddy-hash-here'
```

- Use the LLM variable your `config.yml` expects (`OPENAI_API_KEY` for the default OpenAI setup).
- Keep the **single quotes** around `AUTH_HASH`; the hash contains `$` characters.
- Add `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY=...` only if you test voice (Part 9).

## 🙈 `.gitignore`

In the project root, make sure these lines exist:

```text
.DS_Store
__pycache__/
*.pyc
.venv/
.rasa/
models/
.env
lesson_log.jsonl
```

`models/` and `.rasa/` are large. `.env` holds secrets. `lesson_log.jsonl` holds user IDs and replies.

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint 2:** `deploy/` has three files, and `.gitignore` lists `.env`, `models/`, and `lesson_log.jsonl`.
:::

## 🧪 Part 3 · Run the official image locally

This proves the **container + your project + your keys** work before you use Azure.

```bash
cp deploy/.env.example deploy/.env      # then fill RASA_LICENSE and your LLM key
```

From the project root (needs a trained `models/` folder):

```bash
docker run --rm --user root -p 5005:5005 -v "$PWD":/app --env-file deploy/.env \
  europe-west3-docker.pkg.dev/rasa-releases/rasa-pro/rasa-pro:3.18.0 run --inspect
```

PowerShell: replace `\` with a backtick and `"$PWD"` with `"${PWD}"`.

## 👀 Part 3 · Open the Inspector

- Read the log for a line like *Development inspector for channel rest is running* and the URL that follows.
- Open that URL in your browser. It points at `http://localhost:5005`.
- Run the first steps of the Lab 3 test script: choose a lesson, walk through, say "stuck".
- Stop with `Ctrl+C`.

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint 3:** The Inspector chat works against the **Docker** container, and `lesson_log.jsonl` appears in your project folder.
:::

## ② Put it on GitHub and Azure {.section-slide background-color="#263b3e"}

::: {.eyebrow}
Parts 4–7 · Repo, account, VM, Docker
:::

**Push → budget → VM → ports → Docker**

## 🐙 Part 4 · Publish the repo

1. GitHub Desktop: **File → Add Local Repository…** and pick `AppCoach_demo` (or **create a repository** if asked).
2. In **Changes**, you must see `actions/`, `data/`, `domain.yml`, `config.yml`, `endpoints.yml`, `credentials.yml`, `deploy/`, `.gitignore`.
3. You must **not** see `models/`, `.rasa/`, `deploy/.env`, or `lesson_log.jsonl`.
4. Summary: `Initial commit` → **Commit to main** → **Publish repository**.

> Choose **private** unless you are sure the content is fine to share.

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint 4:** The repo is on github.com with `deploy/docker-compose.yml`, and no `.env` or `models/`.
:::

## 🎓 Part 5 · Free Azure credit

Pick one option.

| Option | What you get | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| **Azure for Students** | About 100 USD credit and free services for 12 months; no credit card | A school email address |
| **Azure free account** | 12 months of free services plus a starter credit | A credit or debit card |

- <https://azure.microsoft.com/free/students>
- <https://azure.microsoft.com/free>

Offers change. Check the pages before you start.

## 💸 Part 5 · Budget first

1. Portal: **Cost Management + Billing → Budgets**. Create a **5 USD budget** with an email alert.
2. A VM shut down from the operating system **still bills**. Use **deallocate** (Part 10).

**Size note:** the free VM allowance covers a 1 GB machine. Rasa Pro needs more, so this workshop uses a **4 GB** VM that is paid from **credit**. Rasa's own quick-deploy guide says 1 vCPU and 2 GB RAM can be enough for a CALM assistant; 4 GB gives margin for training and the image.

## 🖥️ Part 6 · Create the VM

Use **Azure Cloud Shell**: no installation.

1. Sign in to <https://portal.azure.com>.
2. Click the `>_` icon and choose **Bash**.
3. Accept the storage prompt if it appears.

## 🏷️ 6.1 · Pick unique names

Replace `yourname` with lowercase letters and numbers. The DNS label must be unique in the region.

```bash
RG=appcoach-rg
VM=appcoach-vm
LOC=westus2
DNS=appcoach-yourname
```

## 🧰 6.2 · Resource group and VM

```bash
az group create --name $RG --location $LOC

az vm create \
  --resource-group $RG \
  --name $VM \
  --image Ubuntu2404 \
  --size Standard_B2s \
  --admin-username azureuser \
  --generate-ssh-keys \
  --public-ip-sku Standard \
  --public-ip-address-dns-name $DNS
```

If the size is unavailable, list sizes and pick one with **at least 2 GB RAM**:

```bash
az vm list-skus --location $LOC --size Standard_B2 --output table
```

## 🔓 6.3 · Open ports and get the address

```bash
az vm open-port --resource-group $RG --name $VM --port 80  --priority 900
az vm open-port --resource-group $RG --name $VM --port 443 --priority 901
az vm show -d --resource-group $RG --name $VM --query fqdns -o tsv
```

Port 80 is needed for the certificate check. The address looks like `appcoach-yourname.westus2.cloudapp.azure.com`. **Write it down.**

If empty, build it: `$DNS.$LOC.cloudapp.azure.com`.

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint 6:** You have a `*.cloudapp.azure.com` name.
:::

## 🔑 Part 7 · Log in and install Docker

```bash
ssh azureuser@$DNS.$LOC.cloudapp.azure.com
```

Type `yes` to trust the host. Then on the VM:

```bash
sudo apt-get update
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sudo sh
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER
exit
```

**Log in again**, then check `docker --version` and `docker compose version`.

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint 7:** Both commands print a version and `docker ps` works without `sudo`.
:::

## ③ Deploy and verify {.section-slide background-color="#a93632"}

::: {.eyebrow}
Parts 8–9 · Code, secrets, model, HTTPS
:::

**Clone → secrets → train → launch → test**

## 📥 Part 8 · Get the code onto the VM

**Public repo:**

```bash
cd ~
git clone https://github.com/YOUR_GITHUB_USER/AppCoach_demo.git appcoach-demo
```

Use your real username. The repo name is **case-sensitive**.

**Private repo:** use a **deploy key**: read-only access for this one VM and this one repo.

## 🗝️ Private repo · Deploy key

On the VM:

```bash
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "azure-vm" -f ~/.ssh/deploy_key -N ""
cat ~/.ssh/deploy_key.pub
```

On GitHub: repo **Settings → Deploy keys → Add deploy key**. Paste the line. Leave **Allow write access unchecked**.

## 🗝️ Private repo · Use the key

```bash
cat >> ~/.ssh/config <<'EOF'
Host github.com
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/deploy_key
  IdentitiesOnly yes
EOF
chmod 600 ~/.ssh/config
ssh -T git@github.com
cd ~
git clone git@github.com:YOUR_GITHUB_USER/AppCoach_demo.git appcoach-demo
```

Expect: `Hi USER/REPO! You've successfully authenticated`.

## 🔐 8.1 · Make the password hash

On the VM, create the login for the Inspector. The password is not saved in history:

```bash
read -s -p "Choose a password: " PW; echo
docker run --rm caddy:2 caddy hash-password --plaintext "$PW"
```

Copy the whole line that starts with `$2a$`. That is the hash.

> Pick a long password you do not reuse elsewhere. Share it with classmates only if they need access.

## 🔑 8.2 · Create the real `.env`

```bash
cd ~/appcoach-demo/deploy
cp .env.example .env
nano .env
```

Fill in:

- `RASA_LICENSE` and your LLM key
- `DOMAIN` = the exact address from step 6.3
- `AUTH_USER` and `AUTH_HASH='...'` (keep the single quotes)

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint 8:** `deploy/.env` exists on the VM, and `git status` does not list it (it is ignored).
:::

## 🧠 Part 9 · Train on the VM

`models/` is not in git, so train once on the server. Use the **same Rasa version** you tested:

```bash
cd ~/appcoach-demo/deploy
docker compose run --rm assistant train
ls ../models
```

You should see a `.tar.gz` model file. Training calls your LLM provider, so it uses your key.

::: {.notes}
Alternative: train locally and copy the model into ~/appcoach-demo/models on the VM with scp. That needs your SSH key on the laptop, and the key above was generated in Cloud Shell, so training on the VM is simpler.
:::

## 🚀 9.1 · Launch with HTTPS

```bash
docker compose up -d
docker compose ps
docker compose logs -f caddy
```

- After about a minute, Caddy reports that it **obtained a certificate**.
- Press `Ctrl+C` to stop reading logs. The containers keep running.
- Check the assistant: `docker compose logs assistant` should show the server running and the Inspector message.

## 🔎 9.2 · Open the Inspector

Replace `DOMAIN` with your address:

```text
https://DOMAIN/webhooks/rest/inspect.html?projectUrl=https%3A%2F%2FDOMAIN&channel=rest
```

1. Enter `AUTH_USER` and your password when the browser asks.
2. Run the Lab 3 test script: choose a lesson, walk through, **stuck**, **where am I**, **done**, practice mode.

> `projectUrl` must be the **public https address**. The `localhost` URL in the log only works on the VM.

## 🩺 9.3 · Test from the command line

```bash
curl -u coach -s -X POST https://DOMAIN/webhooks/rest/webhook \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"sender":"t1","message":"I want to learn an app"}'
```

- `-u coach` asks for the password; use your own `AUTH_USER`.
- Expect JSON that includes the question **"Which app would you like to learn?"** and its buttons.
- Without `-u`, Caddy answers **401**. That is the password gate working.

## 📝 9.4 · Read the log

After finishing one lesson in the Inspector:

```bash
cat ~/appcoach-demo/lesson_log.jsonl
```

You should see `lesson_started`, `step_shown`, `reply_...`, and `lesson_completed` events.

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint 9:** You completed a guided lesson, a stuck-and-recover turn, and a "where am I" digression at the **https** address, and the log shows the events.
:::

## 🎙️ Optional · Voice

Voice is **not** required for this workshop. If you want to try it:

1. Add `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY=...` to `deploy/.env`.
2. Recreate the assistant: `docker compose up -d --force-recreate assistant`.
3. In the Inspector, switch to voice and allow the microphone.

HTTPS is already in place, which browsers require. Voice over this proxy is **not verified in this deck**: record what works and what fails, including misheard words.

## ④ Operate and wrap up {.section-slide background-color="#0067b8"}

::: {.eyebrow}
Part 10 · Update, stop, clean up, review
:::

**Update → deallocate → delete → reflect**

## 🔄 Part 10 · Deploy an update

On your laptop: edit, commit, **Push origin**. Then on the VM:

```bash
cd ~/appcoach-demo && git pull
cd deploy
docker compose run --rm assistant train
docker compose restart assistant
```

- Changed only `lessons.py` or `actions.py`? Restart is enough; retrain only when `domain.yml`, `flows.yml`, or `config.yml` change.
- The bind mount means **no image rebuild** is needed.

## 🛑 Stop, restart, delete

Azure bills for compute while a VM is **allocated**, even if the OS is shut down:

```bash
az vm deallocate --resource-group appcoach-rg --name appcoach-vm
az vm start      --resource-group appcoach-rg --name appcoach-vm
```

When the course ends, delete everything:

```bash
az group delete --name appcoach-rg --yes
```

Containers with `restart: unless-stopped` come back after a start.

## 🧯 Troubleshooting · Rasa

| Symptom | Likely cause → Fix |
|---|---|
| License error at startup | `RASA_LICENSE` missing or misspelled in `deploy/.env` |
| "No model found" | Training not done → `docker compose run --rm assistant train` |
| Model/version warning | Image tag differs from the version you tested → align the tag, retrain |
| Replies fail or LLM errors | LLM key missing or wrong name → check `config.yml`, update `.env`, recreate |
| Unknown or failing action | `docker compose logs assistant`; check `actions/__init__.py` and `endpoints.yml` |
| Inspector loads but cannot connect | `projectUrl` is `localhost` → use the public https address |

## 🧯 Troubleshooting · Network and login

| Symptom | Likely cause → Fix |
|---|---|
| Browser cannot connect | Ports 80/443 not open → rerun both `az vm open-port` commands |
| Certificate error or timeout | Not issued yet, or wrong `DOMAIN` → `docker compose logs caddy`, `cat .env` |
| Login rejected | Wrong user or hash → regenerate hash; keep single quotes in `.env` |
| Caddy fails to start | Hash pasted wrongly → check `AUTH_USER` and `AUTH_HASH` lines |
| `permission denied` on `docker` | No re-login after `usermod` → `exit`, log in again |
| `variable DOMAIN is not set` | No `deploy/.env` → create it (Part 8) |
| `port is already allocated` | Another service uses 80/443 → `sudo ss -tlnp` |

## 🛡️ Security and privacy checklist

- [ ] SSH uses a key, not a password
- [ ] Only ports 22, 80, and 443 are open
- [ ] Rasa port 5005 is **not** published; only Caddy is
- [ ] The Inspector URL asks for a password
- [ ] `.env`, `models/`, `.rasa/`, and `lesson_log.jsonl` are not in git
- [ ] `rasa run` runs **without** `--enable-api`
- [ ] A budget alert exists
- [ ] You know who can read `lesson_log.jsonl`, and you delete it when the course ends

## 💭 Reflection · Agency and care

1. The log holds a sender ID and every reply. What would **informed consent** look like for an older adult?
2. The Inspector is a developer tool. What would a **real user interface** need that it lacks?
3. The password gate protects your LLM bill. What else could go wrong if the URL is shared?
4. A completed step means the user said "done". Is that evidence they learned the task?

## 📇 Command cheat sheet

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| Train | `cd ~/appcoach-demo/deploy && docker compose run --rm assistant train` |
| Start | `docker compose up -d` |
| Status | `docker compose ps` |
| Logs | `docker compose logs -f assistant` (or `caddy`) |
| Restart Rasa | `docker compose restart assistant` |
| Stop | `docker compose down` |
| Update | `cd ~/appcoach-demo && git pull` |
| Deallocate | `az vm deallocate -g appcoach-rg -n appcoach-vm` |
| Delete all | `az group delete -n appcoach-rg --yes` |

## 📬 Deliverable

Submit:

1. The GitHub repo URL.
2. Your live `https://` URL (do **not** post the password).
3. A screenshot of the Inspector showing a completed lesson at your Azure address.
4. A redacted excerpt of `lesson_log.jsonl`.
5. A short note: **one thing that went wrong and how you fixed it.**

> A deployed assistant is one you can update, protect, and shut down.
